chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa', from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:

It was said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'For what reason did God make the zakat twenty-five in every thousand, and why did He not make it thirty?' So he said: 'God, Mighty and Majestic, made it twenty-five —
taken from the wealth of the rich in the measure of what suffices the poor. And if people were to pay out the zakat from their wealth, no one would be needy.'

key_terms.الزَّكَاة: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax, one of the pillars of Islam
key_terms.الْأَغْنِيَاء: The wealthy/rich — those obligated to pay zakat
key_terms.الْفُقَرَاء: The poor/needy — those entitled to receive zakat
key_terms.خَمْسَةً وَعِشْرِينَ فِي كُلِّ أَلْفٍ: Twenty-five in every thousand — the zakat rate of 2.5%
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God

ai.seo_question: Why is zakat set at 2.5% (25 per thousand) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) transmits that Imam al-Sadiq (AS) was asked why zakat is set at 2.5% (25 per 1000) and not 3%. The Imam explains that God calibrated the zakat rate precisely: 25 parts per thousand from the wealth of the rich is exactly the measure that, if properly distributed, would eliminate poverty entirely. The statement is both a jurisprudential clarification and a profound social observation — that God's divine wisdom in setting zakat at this level is sufficient to sustain all the poor, provided people comply.
